preamble: Lands here are 4-ed (as our non-PC forebears would think) by 14 down

clue.text: Goings on at home may, if I fell, change

indicators.note: change is an imperative here, telling the solver to rearrange the preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone warns that domestic arrangements would be upset if they took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns MAYIFIFELL, the letters of 'may, if I fell', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic routine and the doings of a household are what people mean by this phrase.

clue.text: A sticky object — that's me — means one can be either too young or too old

definitions.text: one can be either too young or too old

parts.note: gel is a sticky substance, as in hair gel
the speaker saying 'that's me' gives I'M
it is a pronoun used as an object, a thing

explanation.surface: A speaker describes themselves as some gummy item, then shifts to talk of people being the wrong age.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in answer order with 'that's me' slotted between the sticky stuff and the object; 'means' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off of years either side means a person may be ruled out for youth or for seniority.

clue.text: Hospital worker, say, one after another

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the hospital worker is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor

explanation.surface: A hospital worker is described, then the clue drifts into talk of sequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things successively, each following the last, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: See 14
They come out from underground, given lift when poet's about

indicators.note: about means the poet's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet; with the 's it gives DANTES

indicators.note: given lift, in a down clue, means the word is raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Creatures emerge from a burrow and are raised up while a poet hovers nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given lift' reverses the underground railway in this down clue, and 'about' puts the poet round it; the definition plays on debutantes 'coming out' into society.
explanation.definitionFit: Debutantes traditionally 'come out' into society at their first formal season.

clue.text: Telepathy leads to recipe with petrol to drink

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, covers telepathy
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, 'take')
Esso is a brand of petrol

explanation.surface: Mind-reading somehow results in a recipe calling for fuel as a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee is a kind of drink.

clue.text: A new identification for Currie?

parts.note: The clue hints that her first name is simply the letters of 'a new' plus ID, a fresh identity for her

explanation.walkthrough: Edwina Currie was a British Conservative MP and minister. The clue is a cryptic definition: her first name is literally 'a new ID' shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to the politician's first name, which reworks the letters of 'a new ID'.

clue.text: 1 in 100? On the contrary, far less often

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, here reversed by the following phrase
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the hundred goes inside the one rather than the one inside the hundred

parts.note: 1 is ONE
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a probability of one in a hundred, saying it happens much more rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 in 100' reads as ONE inside C, but 'On the contrary' flips it: C goes inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening a single time is far rarer than happening repeatedly.

clue.text: Land of composer entertaining fellow setter

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the guests within, so the composer's name goes round the rest

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of 'Rule, Britannia!'
a gent is a fellow
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A country associated with a composer who plays host to a man and the crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble notes such lands once took 'the': the Argentine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine is the old name for Argentina, a South American country.

clue.text: Land — the Midi — for its year

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France, and sud is French for south
in the Midi's own language, French, a year is an

explanation.surface: A place is likened to southern France, offered in exchange for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' means the Midi's language, French, so both pieces are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is an African country, once called the Sudan.

clue.text: Selective killing returned in kind, as maybe this would have it

definitions.text: as maybe this would have it

indicators.note: in places the reversed killing inside the word for kind

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort

indicators.note: returned means the word for the killing is read backwards

parts.note: a cull is a selective slaughter of animals

explanation.surface: A selective slaughter is repaid in the same way, as fate might decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the killing, and 'in' sets it inside the word for kind; the definition fills the blank in the stock phrase 'as ___ would have it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as misfortune would have it' fills the blank: the answer slots into 'as ___ would have it'.

clue.text: Land of ours — weather English, too

parts.note: for a British paper, our country is the UK
rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: A country is said to share British weather, English too.
explanation.walkthrough: Once often called the Ukraine, as the preamble's old-fashioned forebears would have it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is an Eastern European country.

clue.text: Land where people were addressed

parts.note: ye is the old word by which a group of people were addressed
men are people

explanation.surface: A country where folk were once spoken to in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye men!' is an archaic form of address; 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula, formerly the Yemen.

clue.text: Land, variant — Natal's variant

indicators.note: the second variant asks for a variant form, a rearrangement, of the letters before it

parts.note: var is the abbreviation for variant
Natal's gives its letters including the S

explanation.surface: A region described as an alternative version of the South African province Natal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variant' first gives VAR; the second 'variant' shuffles VAR with NATALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transvaal was a South African province, a land often given 'the'.

clue.text: Think about English girl in goal, first and last with supposed ancestor

indicators.note: about means the word think goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
taken as written

indicators.note: first and last asks for the outer letters of the word goal

explanation.surface: Someone muses on an English girl keeping goal, the first and last ones linked to a mythical forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the opening word split open round the other pieces, and 'first and last' takes only the outer letters of goal. The preamble's 4-ed is 'linked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hypothetical creature bridging apes and humans is a supposed ancestor of mankind.

clue.text: Table including a politician in the nude I attack personally

indicators.note: including means the table holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a list is a table
MP, Member of Parliament
being in the nude means having nothing (O) on (ON)

explanation.surface: A naked politician turns up on a chart, and the speaker makes it a personal assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the nude' is read as 'nothing on', giving O and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist who ridicules individuals would describe themselves as attacking personally.

clue.text: Nanny's policy is to put flue underground where I and Salmon play

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Nanny's policy is to put flue underground where I and Salmon play'. INTER + VENT is clear but IONISM cannot come from 'I and Salmon' (it would need I and SIMON); the printed text could not be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Nanny's policy is to put flue underground where I and Salmon play

clue.text: Started again to write on love among climbing animals

indicators.note: among means set inside the other piece
climbing, in a down clue, means the word goes up, read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals

indicators.note: on means put next to the love, after it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A writer resumes, penning amorous lines amid scrambling creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the animals bottom to top in this down clue, 'on' puts the pen after the love, and 'among' sets that pair inside the reversed animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen is to open again, so having reopened is having started again.

clue.text: One ninth's infraction — leave car at Hackney pub

indicators.note: an infraction breaks something, so the words before are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives no letter, just NINTH
to park is to leave a car

explanation.surface: A breach of rules by one ninth, then parking near a London pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infraction' rearranges ONENINTH into INNONTHE. Hackney is a London borough; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inn on the Park is the name of a pub in Hackney, London.

clue.text: Nice noises made by Brussels charlatans?

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union
phonies are fakes or charlatans

explanation.surface: Pleasant sounds are made by fraudsters at the European headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' means pleasant here, not the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is a pleasing sound, so its plural is agreeable noises.

clue.text: Land of wordplay and inoculation

parts.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay
a jab is an inoculation

explanation.surface: A country known for puns and vaccinations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Punjab is a region straddling India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Land with activity on the other side

indicators.note: on means placed after the other side

parts.note: con means against, the opposing side, as in pros and cons
go means activity or energy

explanation.surface: A country where things happen on the opposite bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a central African country.

clue.text: Copper and singer changing 2 to 8, say

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Bing Crosby was an American singer

explanation.surface: A policeman and a crooner alter the numbers two and eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising 2 to the third power makes 8, an example of the operation.

clue.text: Tool for prince's use

indicators.note: use suggests putting the letters to another use, reworking them

parts.note: the letters of prince's, including the S

explanation.surface: A tool made for royal use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' rearranges PRINCES; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pincers are a gripping tool with two jaws.

clue.text: See 18
Land of prohibition entering sign on pole

indicators.note: entering means the prohibition goes inside the sign

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a ban is a prohibition
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A country where a ban is imposed on a sign at a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link setting the pole next to the sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern country, once often called the Lebanon.

clue.text: Opening for pen friend up in the far North

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: opening for means the first letter of the word pen

explanation.surface: A pen pal is sought somewhere up in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the friend in this down clue and 'Opening for' takes the first letter of pen; the definition stands for a person who lives in the far North.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is a native of Lapland, someone living in the far North of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Victorian novelist and what to do with him, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the word is said aloud, matching the novelist's name

parts.note: what you do with a novelist's book is read it

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist and advice on how to treat him.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade wrote novels in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Drug (confined to heroin) seen returning thereabouts

indicators.note: thereabouts means around, so the reversed word surrounds the rest
returning means the word seen is read backwards

parts.note: pent means shut in or confined
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug, restricted to heroin, is seen coming back somewhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes SEEN into NEES, which 'thereabouts' wraps round PENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthes, or nepenthe, is a legendary drug of forgetfulness.
